rationale: Both reviews are exceptionally thorough and well-evidenced, and both independently catch GT's second-highest-severity finding (v2 codec silently swallowing legacy checkpoints via shared model_type) plus the WER PCM-fallback issue. But on GT's single highest-confidence finding — stream slots leaking because release is only reached via the finished/stream_finished payload path (confirmed and fixed by the author) — X explicitly asserts the abort-release path already works correctly, actively missing/contradicting it, while Y independently flags the same slot-leak failure mode (via an id-space mismatch in on_requests_finished) in the same function. Y also catches the docstring-staleness item GT calls out; X does not. Both are equally concrete and actionable with file:line evidence, so the gap is driven by recall on the marquee findings rather than precision or actionability.
